title: Relative slices and their coherent sections
statement: Use the universes, smallness, compactness and filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the coherent functors, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Use cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; for an arbitrary simplicial base use the same inner-horn and cocartesian-edge lifting conditions. Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small quasicategory, let $D\subseteq\mathcal C$ be a replete full subcategory, let $K$ be a small simplicial set, and let $p:K\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram. Form the simplicial pullback $E=K\times_{p,\mathcal C,\operatorname{ev}_1}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ and retain those simplices whose source vertices lie in $D$; call the resulting simplicial set $E_D$. The projection $E_D\to K$ is a cocartesian fibration. Its fiber at $v$ is the coherent slice $D_{/p(v)}$, and transport over an edge $e:v\to w$ is postcomposition by $p(e)$. The quasicategory of all sections $\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K,E_D)$ is equivalent to the coherent comma category of pairs $(d,\alpha)$ with $d:K\to D$ and $\alpha:d\to p$ a coherent transformation in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, including its higher simplices. If $D$ is essentially small, this section category and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)$ are essentially small. For every $x\in\mathcal C$, the source functor $\mathcal C_{/x}\to\mathcal C$ creates every colimit whose underlying source diagram has a colimit in $\mathcal C$. If a class of diagram shapes has colimits in $\mathcal C$ and $D$ is closed under these colimits in $\mathcal C$, then the corresponding colimits exist in $D_{/x}$, are computed on sources, and postcomposition $D_{/x}\to D_{/y}$ preserves them for every arrow $x\to y$.
